hindi: और भी जो कुछ वृद्ध स्त्रियाँ कहें।
english: And whatever else old women may also say.
notes: GROUPING: appears to be the tail of a longer statement (what old women say) whose main clause lies outside this unit; the sentence is left open here.

words.gloss: stretched out (pratāna); lying face up (uttāna); sleeping
nāḍī (channel, vessel; here probably the umbilical cord, probable)

hindi: तानकर और उत्तान यानी चित सोने वाली के गर्भ की, नाभि पर टिकी नाड़ी, जो सम्भवतः गर्भनाल है, फिर कण्ठ को लपेटकर विपत्ति करती है।
english: For a woman who sleeps stretched out and face up, again, the fetus's nāḍī (probably the umbilical cord), resting on the navel, having wound around the neck, causes a mishap (vyāpatti).

text_flags.why: possible: nābhyāśrayā is feminine nominative, so the subject should be nāḍī (nom.); the accusative anusvara looks like a print slip

notes: nāḍī = vessel or channel; reading it as the umbilical cord is probable, not stated in the word itself. 'garbhasya' is taken with nāḍī; whose neck is not stated (the fetus's is the natural reading). 'pratāna' is not firmly known (stretched out); the compound may also be two habits run together, 'sleeping stretched out and sleeping face up'. The genitive of the woman stands loosely ('in the case of').

hindi: बिना ढके सोने वाली और रात में घूमने वाली उन्मत्त को उत्पन्न करती है।
english: She who sleeps uncovered, and she who roams at night, produces a mad (one).
notes: Subject (the pregnant woman) understood from the context. Whether one woman has both habits or either habit suffices is not settled by the wording (singular verb). 'vivṛta' = uncovered, or possibly 'in the open'. unmatta = mad (unmāda, standard). The verb janayati serves the following units 118-134 as well.

hindi: झगड़ालू स्वभाव वाली: अपस्मार यानी मिर्गी वाला।
english: She who is quarrelsome by nature: one with apasmāra (epilepsy).
notes: Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

hindi: व्यवाय यानी मैथुन में लगी रहने वाली: बुरे शरीर वाला, अनुमानित पाठ पर निर्लज्ज, या स्त्रैण।
english: She who is given to sexual intercourse (vyavāya): an ill-shaped, shameless (on a conjectural reading) or womanish (straiṇa) (one).

text_flags.why: possible: 'anhīka' is not a known word; ahrīka (a-hrī-ka, 'without shame') fits the series of faults and a dropped/misread conjunct hrī -> nhī is a plausible OCR error

notes: Hedged: 'ahrīka' is a conjectured reading of the printed 'anhīkaṃ'. 'straiṇa' = womanish, effeminate (it can also mean fond of women); the plainest sense is kept. The three adjectives are read as alternatives, 'or' closing the list. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

hindi: निरन्तर शोक में रहने वाली: डरपोक, क्षीण या अल्पायु।
english: She who is constantly given to grief (śoka): a timid, wasted or short-lived (one).

text_flags.why: near certain: ॉ is a stray vowel sign; 'śoka' (grief) fits the series of X-nityā compounds

notes: apacita = wasted, diminished (it also means 'honoured'; wasted suits the list). The same word occurs in 132. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

hindi: लोभ करने वाली: दूसरों को सन्ताप देने वाला, ईर्ष्यालु या स्त्रैण।
english: She who is covetous: one who torments others, a jealous or womanish (one).
notes: abhidhyā = coveting (longing for another's possession). 'paropatāpana' = causing distress to others. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

hindi: चोर स्त्री तो: परिश्रम से भरा, द्रोही या अकर्मशील।
english: She who is a thief, however: one abounding in toil (āyāsa), hostile, or given to inaction (akarma).
notes: The printed run-together first word is split as stenā tu āyāsabahulam abhidrohiṇam akarmaśīlam; 'tu' is the odd element (it contrasts with the preceding habits) and the split is probable, not certain. 'akarmaśīla' could also mean 'given to wrong action'; the literal 'inaction' is kept. 'abhidrohin' = hostile/injurious to others. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

hindi: असहनशील: उग्र या सम्भवतः कपटी।
english: She who is intolerant: a fierce or probably deceitful (aupadhika) (one).
notes: aupadhika: 'deceitful, practising upadhi (trick, fraud)' is probable; the word has other senses ('additional'), so it is hedged. The print joins 'vā' to the previous word (aupadhikaṃvā); split here without a flag as a spacing slip. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: small; fire (agni); alpāgni = weak digestive fire, poor digestion (standard)

hindi: सोने के स्वभाव वाली: उनींदा, नासमझ या अल्प अग्नि यानी मन्द पाचन वाला।
english: She who is given to sleep: a drowsy, foolish (one), or one with small fire (agni), weak digestion.
notes: svapna = sleep here (it can also mean dream). Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

hindi: मद्य यानी मादक पेय में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: अत्यधिक प्यास वाला, अल्प स्मृति वाला या अस्थिर।
english: She who is constantly given to madya (an intoxicating drink): one prone to thirst, of poor memory, or unsteady.
notes: tṛṣṇālu could also mean craving (tṛṣṇā in general); 'prone to thirst' is the plainer sense. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: monitor lizard (godhā, standard; the species, probably Varanus bengalensis, is probable); flesh; constant in

hindi: गोधा यानी गोह के मांस में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: अश्मरी यानी पथरी वाला, या धीरे मूत्र करने वाला।
english: She who is constantly given to godhā-flesh (meat of the monitor lizard): one with aśmarī (urinary stone), or one who passes urine slowly.
notes: Printed with avagraha (godhāmāṃsanityā'śmariṇaṃ) = nityā aśmariṇam. 'śanair-mehin' is taken as 'passing urine slowly (in a trickle)'; mehin could also mean 'one with meha (urinary disorder)', so the sense is not firm. Hedged identification: godhā = monitor lizard standard, exact species probable. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: wild boar or pig (varāha; standard); flesh; constant in

hindi: वराह यानी सूअर के मांस में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: लाल आँखों वाला, क्रथन जिसका अर्थ अनिश्चित है, या अत्यन्त कठोर रोमों वाला।
english: She who is constantly given to varāha-flesh (meat of the wild boar or pig): a red-eyed (one), a krathana (sense uncertain), or one with very rough hair.
notes: 'krathana' is kept untranslated: a rare word (possibly from √krath 'to hurt', or a sound-word), not enriched. 'varāha' = boar/pig (standard). The last compound is a bahuvrīhi in -roman (acc. -romāṇam). Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

hindi: मछली के मांस में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: देर से पलक झपकाने वाला या जड़ आँखों वाला।
english: She who is constantly given to fish-flesh: one with slow blinking, or a stiff-eyed (one).
notes: 'ciranimeṣa' = slow in blinking (literally 'long wink'); 'stabdhākṣa' = stiff or staring eyes. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: sweet (madhura, the sweet taste); constant in
one with prameha (a group of urinary disorders; diabetes-type probable)

hindi: मधुर यानी मीठे में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: प्रमेह यानी सम्भवतः मधुमेह की प्रकृति की मूत्र-व्याधि वाला, गूँगा या अत्यन्त स्थूल।
english: She who is constantly given to the sweet (madhura): one with prameha (a group of urinary disorders, probably diabetes-type), a mute, or a very stout (one).
notes: Printed 'madhurānityā' = madhurā-nityā (madhura as a taste, rasa, in feminine form agreeing with the noun-less 'taste') and 'mūkamatisthūlaṃvā' joins vā. Identification of prameha as diabetes-type: probable. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: sour (amla, the sour taste); constant in
raktapitta (a bleeding disorder; probable); one with it

hindi: अम्ल यानी खट्टे में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: रक्तपित्त यानी सम्भवतः रक्तस्राव की व्याधि वाला, या त्वचा और आँखों के रोग वाला।
english: She who is constantly given to the sour (amla): one with raktapitta (a bleeding disorder, probable), or one with diseases of skin and eyes.
notes: raktapitta = bleeding from body openings, probable as the modern sense. 'tvagakṣirogin' is read as 'one with disease of skin and of eyes'. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: salty (lavaṇa, the salt taste); constant in

hindi: लवण यानी नमकीन में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: शीघ्र झुर्रियों और पलित यानी बाल पकने वाला, या गंजा।
english: She who is constantly given to the salty (lavaṇa): one with early wrinkles (valī) and greying (palita), or a bald (one).
notes: Printed 'balī' for valī (v/b interchange, normalised). khalatika = bald (baldness, standard). Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: bitter (tikta, the bitter taste); constant in
one with śoṣa (wasting disease; consumption-type, probable)

hindi: तिक्त यानी कड़वे में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: शोष यानी सम्भवतः क्षय की प्रकृति की सूखने वाली व्याधि वाला, दुर्बल या क्षीण।
english: She who is constantly given to the bitter (tikta): one with śoṣa (a wasting disease, probably consumption-type), a weak, or a wasted (one).
notes: śoṣa = drying, wasting; the consumption-type sense is probable. apacita as in 120. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: pungent (kaṭuka, the pungent taste); constant in

hindi: कटुक यानी तीखे में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: दुर्बल, अल्प शुक्र यानी वीर्य नामक प्रजनन-द्रव वाला, या सन्तानहीन।
english: She who is constantly given to the pungent (kaṭuka): a weak (one), one with little śukra (semen), or one without offspring.
notes: The printed 'durvalam' is an accepted spelling variant of durbala; no flag. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gloss: astringent (kaṣāya, the astringent taste); constant in
one with ānāha (distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind; standard)
one with udāvarta (reversed, upward course of Vāta; standard)

hindi: कसैले में नित्य लगी रहने वाली: श्याम यानी साँवला, आनाह यानी पेट फूलने और मल रुकने वाला, या उदावर्त यानी वायु के उलटे ऊपर चढ़ने की व्याधि वाला।
english: She who is constantly given to the astringent (kaṣāya): a dusky (one), one with ānāha (distension of the belly with retention), or one with udāvarta (a disorder in which Vāta runs upward).
notes: kaṣāya here is the taste (astringent), not a decoction. Printed 'śyāmamānāhinamudāvartinaṃ' = śyāmam ānāhinam udāvartinam. Elliptical: the verb janayati (produces) is carried from unit 117 and is not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. 'nityā' = constant in, given to.

words.gram: pres. mid. part. ā-√sev, f. nom. sg.

hindi: जो-जो जिस रोग का निदान है, उस-उसका सेवन करती हुई अन्तर्वत्नी यानी गर्भवती स्त्री उन-उन विकारों से भरपूर सन्तान को जन्म देती है।
english: Whatever is the cause (nidāna) of whatever disease, the pregnant woman (antarvatnī) who indulges in each of those begets offspring abounding in the corresponding disorders.

text_flags.why: possible: āsevamānāṃ (acc.) does not agree with the nominative strī/antarvatnī; the anusvara looks like a print slip for ā

notes: Token 'tattadāsevamānāṃ'tarvatnī' = tat-tat āsevamānā antarvatnī (avagraha printed for a-). 'nidāna' = cause (of disease, standard). apatya is neuter. The Sanskrit says 'each of those', 'cause' is not repeated.

hindi: इससे पिता से उत्पन्न शुक्र के दोष भी बताए गए हैं।
english: By this, the faults of śukra (semen) that are born of the father are also explained.
notes: Printed 'pitṛjā apiśukradoṣā' = pitṛjāḥ api śukra-doṣāḥ (regular visarga loss). 'etena' refers back to the preceding account of the mother's habits. doṣa = fault here, not the humour.

hindi: इसलिए सन्तान की सम्पन्नता चाहने वाले दोनों अपनी भली प्रकार देखभाल करें।
english: Therefore the two, wishing for success of offspring (prajā-sampad), should look after themselves well.
notes: The dual subject is 'the two' (in the context, the couple); the text does not name them in this line. 'ātmānam' is singular (each one's self).

words.gram: m. inst. sg. used as ind.

hindi: विशेष रूप से नारी।
english: Especially the woman (nārī).
notes: Elliptical: the verb of 137 (upācaretām) or a similar verb is understood and not supplied. GROUPING: appears to continue 137.

hindi: और इसके रोगों का मृदु, मधुर, शीतल और सुखकर औषध, आहार और विहार से उपचार करना चाहिए।
english: And one should treat her diseases with mild, sweet, cool and pleasant medicines (auṣadha), foods and regimens (vihāra).

text_flags.why: certain: the prefix is upa-ā-√car with short u; long ū in 'airūpācaret' is a print slip

notes: vihāra = regimen or conduct (daily activities). The four adjectives are read as qualifying all three nouns. 'asyāḥ' written 'asyā' by regular sandhi.

hindi: और इसके लिए वमन आदि का प्रयोग नहीं करना चाहिए।
english: And one should not apply to her emesis (vamana) and the rest.
notes: vamana = therapeutic emesis; 'ādi' = and the other cleansing procedures, not listed here. Genitive 'asyāḥ' taken as 'to/for her'.

hindi: रक्तावसेचन नहीं; किन्तु केवल आठवें मास से आरम्भ करके आस्थापन यानी काढ़े की बस्ति या अनुवासन यानी तेल की बस्ति।
english: Not bloodletting (raktāvasecana); but only, beginning from the eighth month, āsthāpana (decoction enema) or anuvāsana (oil enema).

text_flags.why: possible: doubled t in 'rakttā-' is not a spelling of rakta-avasecana; likely a print slip

notes: Elliptical: the verb of 140 (prayojayet) is understood and not supplied. The wording does not settle whether the enemas are an exception to the prohibitions or a continuing prohibition; the literal sequence is kept ('but only ... from the eighth month'). Enema identifications are standard.

words.gloss: emesis; and the rest; curable by

hindi: और वमन आदि से साध्य विकारों में फिर मृदु या उसी प्रयोजन को पूरा करने वालों से उपक्रम करना चाहिए।
english: But in disorders curable by emesis (vamana) and the rest, one should proceed with mild (ones) or with those that accomplish the same purpose.
notes: Printed 'mṛdubhistadarthakāribhirvopakramet' = mṛdubhiḥ tad-artha-kāribhiḥ vā upakramet. The means are not named ('(ones)'). upakrama = beginning of treatment.

words.gram: pres. part. caus. saṃ-√kṣubh, m. nom. sg.

hindi: तेल से भरे पात्र की तरह, बिना हिलाए गर्भिणी की सेवा करनी चाहिए।
english: Like a full vessel of oil, one should attend to the pregnant woman (garbhiṇī) without shaking (her).
notes: The object of asaṃkṣobhayan is understood (her, or by the simile the vessel); '(her)' is supplied only for readability. The closing 'iti' ends the prose passage and is not translated.

hindi: और इस विषय में ये हैं।
english: And on this matter there are these.
notes: Standard lead-in formula, 'and on this there are (verses)'; the noun is not stated in the Sanskrit and is not supplied. It introduces the verses that follow (145 onward).

hindi: इस प्रकार अनात्ययिक रोग में विधि; किन्तु अत्यधिक में।
english: Thus the rule in a non-critical (anātyayika) disease; but in a very severe (one)
notes: Left elliptical: no copula is supplied. 'atyadhike' agrees with an understood vyādhau. The sentence runs on into 146 (146 appears to complete 145 as one verse of two lines; this pairing is not stated by the print).

hindi: तीक्ष्ण चिकित्सा-प्रयोगों से भी स्त्री की यत्न से रक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: Even with sharp applications of treatment (kriyāyoga), one should carefully protect the woman.
notes: Continues 145 (appears to complete it). tīkṣṇa = sharp, strong, harsh.

hindi: स्त्री ही सन्तानों की जड़ है; स्त्री ही, रक्षित होने पर, रक्षा करती है।
english: For woman is the root of offspring; for woman, when protected, protects.
notes: The object of rakṣati is not expressed and not supplied. The printed tokens are 'strī hi mūlamapatyānāṃ strī hi rakṣati rakṣitā'. 147-148 appear to pair as one verse; not stated by the print.

hindi: सब आश्रमों में प्रथम, निन्दारहित गृहस्थपन।
english: Of all the āśramas (stages of life), first, blameless, the state of a householder.
notes: Elliptical: no copula supplied. 'prathamam' may also be an adverb ('first'); either way the sense is the same. Appears to belong with 147 as one verse; not stated by the print. The line is not further explained here.

hindi: जरायु से मुख ढके होने पर और कफ से कण्ठ लिपटे होने पर
english: When the mouth is covered by the jarāyu (fetal membrane) and the throat is enveloped by Kapha,
notes: Two locative absolutes; the sentence completes in 150 (150 appears to complete it; not stated by the print). jarāyu = the membrane enclosing the fetus (the exact structure, amnion or chorion, is not given). 'cakaphaveṣṭite' = ca kapha-veṣṭite.

hindi: वायु के मार्ग के रुक जाने से गर्भ में रहने वाला रोता नहीं।
english: And because of obstruction of the path of wind (vāyu), the one staying in the womb does not cry out.
notes: Completes the sentence begun in 149 (appears to). 'garbhastha' = the one in the womb (not further specified). 'vāyu' is the wind or air; it is not read as the humour Vāta here.

hindi: इस प्रकार गर्भावक्रान्ति यानी गर्भ का अवतरण नामक द्वितीय अध्याय
english: Thus the second chapter, named Garbhāvakrānti (the descent of the embryo).
notes: Colophon. The printed tokens 'itigarbhāvakrāṃtirnāma' and 'dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ' are run together by sandhi.
